name: Khaleefa Butti bin Omair Al-Muhairi
current_role: Emirati investor; former vice-chairman and major shareholder of NMC Health (resigned Feb 2020); listed as chairman of Travelex Holding
profile: Abu Dhabi businessman (name also spelled Khalifa Butti Omeir Bin Yousef) who, with partners, built a stake of roughly 40% in UAE hospital group NMC Health, partly by buying shares from founder B.R. Shetty in 2017. He was NMC vice-chairman until February 2020, when he resigned amid the company's collapse. His current activities are not well documented.
interesting_fact: He and partners held about 40% of NMC Health, once a FTSE 100 company, before he resigned as vice-chairman in February 2020.
notes: Sensitive: NMC Health collapsed in a 2020 accounting scandal and AGBI reports he later sought bankruptcy/restructuring via an Abu Dhabi court. Probably not a suitable podcast guest. I found no published contact channels.

name: Liu Qingfeng
current_role: Founder, chairman and president, iFLYTEK Co., Ltd. (Hefei, Shenzhen-listed 002230)
profile: Born 1973 in Tongcheng, Anhui, Liu founded iFLYTEK in 1999 as a second-year PhD student at USTC with a dozen classmates, raising seed funds from the university. iFLYTEK listed in Shenzhen in 2008 and became China's leading speech-recognition and AI company; Liu now drives its 'Spark' large-language-model push.
interesting_fact: He recalls iFLYTEK losing money for its first five years before becoming China's voice-recognition leader.
deep_cut_fact: He entered USTC as an undergraduate in 1990 and, as a doctoral student, developed China's first Mandarin speech-synthesis system (1998), the year before founding iFLYTEK.
notes: taojiang@iflytek.com belongs to board secretary Jiang Tao, as listed in iFLYTEK's English annual report. xunfei@iflytek.com is the company's general email. Liu often speaks at Boao Forum and other Chinese AI events, so the AI and compute-energy angle fits.

name: Simón Pedro Barceló Vadell
current_role: Executive chairman and CEO, Barceló Group (Barceló Corporación Empresarial), Palma de Mallorca
profile: Born in Palma in 1966, he studied law at the University of the Balearic Islands and joined the family tourism group in 1993. He co-chaired it with his cousin Simón Barceló Tous from 2000 and now leads it alone after his cousin's age-limit retirement in 2025. The group, founded in 1931, runs 300+ hotels in about 30 countries plus the Ávoris travel business.
interesting_fact: Barceló started in 1931 as a bus/transport company in Mallorca and opened its first hotel only in 1962. Hosteltur named Simón Pedro Barceló its 2023 Tourism Personality of the Year, marking 30 years at the company.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he was a senator for the Partido Popular from 1989 to 1993, entering the Spanish Senate in his early twenties.
notes: He gives Spanish-media interviews fairly often (Hosteltur, Exceltur forums) and is a former president of the Exceltur tourism lobby. The best route is the group communications office.

name: Warren Chen
current_role: Chairman, DynaColor Inc. (TPEx: 5489); cofounder and shareholder of Chroma ATE
profile: Warren Chen co-founded Chroma ATE (TWSE: 2360) in 1984 with other National Chiao Tung University alumni, including billionaire Leo Huang. Chroma makes automated test equipment for power electronics, EVs and semiconductors, and AI data-center power demand has lifted its shares. In 1991 he founded DynaColor, a Taipei maker of video-surveillance and machine-vision cameras, which he chairs.
interesting_fact: Forbes notes that Chroma's power-testing equipment is increasingly used worldwide as the AI boom drives up electricity demand, which makes him a direct fit for an energy and data-center podcast.
notes: Investing.com and StockAnalysis list a Warren Chen as DynaColor chairman/CEO. MarketScreener names the chairman 'Chun Sheng Chen' (an NCTU graduate), probably his formal name, but I could not confirm that link. He is low-profile, with almost no English press. DynaColor's contact page lists only sales emails; reach him via the company or through Chroma ATE.

name: Chandubhai Virani
current_role: Cofounder and chairman/managing director, Balaji Wafers Pvt. Ltd. (Rajkot, Gujarat)
profile: A farmer's son from Jamnagar district, Virani and his brothers moved to Rajkot in 1974 and worked at the Astron Cinema canteen. In 1982 they began making their own potato wafers, and Balaji grew into one of India's largest regional snack brands. The brothers became billionaires after selling a minority stake to General Atlantic in January 2026.
interesting_fact: For years he turned down stake offers from PepsiCo, General Mills and about 50 private-equity firms, saying he was there to run the company, not sell it. The 2026 General Atlantic minority deal was the family's first outside investment.
deep_cut_fact: At Astron Cinema he earned Rs 90 a month and repaired torn seats after night shows in exchange for a plate of chorafali. He started making wafers after 'changing suppliers three times'.
notes: His Vad plant (2003) ran about 5,000 kg of potatoes per hour, a record at the time. He gives interviews mostly in Gujarati/Hindi media. contact@balajiwafers.com is the company's general inbox.

name: Ted Schwartz
current_role: Co-founder, Strand Equity (Los Angeles family-office-style private equity firm); founder and principal, Schwartz Capital Group
profile: The list entry (Forbes 1996, no source of wealth given) most likely refers to Ted Schwartz, who founded APAC TeleServices/APAC Customer Services in 1973. APAC went public in 1995 and its shares soared in 1996. It grew from phone sales of radio and cable ad time into a call-center outsourcer with 25,000+ staff. He sold his remaining stake to JP Morgan in 2011 and now invests through Strand Equity.
interesting_fact: APAC began by selling brokered radio and cable-TV advertising time by phone and at one point represented over 1,500 radio stations before pivoting to customer-service outsourcing.
deep_cut_fact: He founded APAC in 1973, took it public in 1995, and in 1996 started his own investment firm, TCS Group LLC, later renamed Schwartz Capital Group.
notes: Identity is inferred, since the input has no company. The 1996 Forbes listing matches APAC's post-IPO peak, but I did not confirm it against the archived Forbes 400. Strand Equity lists Ted Schwartz as co-founder alongside partners Todd Schwartz and Tracy Schwartz-Ward.

name: He Renbao
current_role: Co-founder, director and controlling shareholder (with wife Wang Yingmei), Zhejiang Yongtai Technology Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 002326)
profile: He Renbao co-founded Zhejiang Yongtai Technology in 1999 in Linhai, Taizhou, with his wife Wang Yingmei, who chairs it. MarketScreener lists him as founder and director and as CEO from 2007. Yongtai makes fluorinated intermediates for pharmaceuticals and crop protection, plus battery materials such as LiPF6 and LiFSI lithium salts, and has expanded into the EV supply chain.
interesting_fact: Yongtai was the first Shenzhen-listed company to issue GDRs on the London Stock Exchange.
notes: Fortune shared with his wife Wang Yingmei. MarketScreener lists a Kuang He as CEO since 2020, so his current executive title is unclear. He keeps a low profile, and I found no English interviews. zhengquan@ is the securities/investor-relations department inbox. The battery-materials angle (EV electrolyte salts) is relevant to energy.

name: Bruno Rousset
current_role: Founder and chairman, Evolem (Lyon family office); founder of insurance group APRIL
profile: Born 1956 in Tain-l'Hermitage (Drôme), Rousset co-founded insurance broker APRIL in Lyon in 1988 with Xavier Coquard and listed it in Paris in 1997. His holding Evolem sold its controlling stake to CVC in 2019. Evolem now backs SMEs (Plateforme), growth startups (Start, 150+ companies), real estate and philanthropy focused on youth employment and climate.
interesting_fact: In 2020 he set up the Domorrow endowment fund to tackle the climate challenge, and his Evolem Citoyen fund created EDEN School in 2017, described as the first digital school for under-18s.
deep_cut_fact: He started in 1978 as a mutualist adviser at the Mutualité Française, then spent eight years at Lyon pension fund UPESE. In 2006 he helped create Entrepreneurs de la Cité, a foundation offering micro-insurance to entrepreneurs in precarious situations.
notes: Evolem runs a blog, 'Valeurs d'entrepreneurs', and he is accessible to French business media. The climate fund Domorrow is a natural angle for an energy podcast. The X handle comes from Wikidata and I did not check it directly. The personal site brunorousset.com did not respond.

name: Anastasia Soare
current_role: Founder and CEO, Anastasia Beverly Hills (ABH)
profile: Born 1957 in Constanța, Romania, Soare emigrated to Los Angeles in 1989 speaking little English and worked as an aesthetician. She developed a brow-shaping method based on facial bone structure, opened her Bedford Drive salon by 1997 and built Anastasia Beverly Hills, sold in about 2,000 stores. TPG invested in 2018. Known as the 'Eyebrow Queen', she still runs the company.
interesting_fact: She has said her first eyebrow clients were Cindy Crawford and Naomi Campbell. She had to rent a room in a Beverly Hills salon after her manager doubted there was a market for eyebrow shaping.
deep_cut_fact: Before emigrating she studied art history and architecture in Romania. She based her brow-shaping method on proportions from that training, fitting brows to each person's bone structure.
notes: The Instagram and X accounts belong to the company, not to her personally. Forbes listed her as a billionaire only in 2019; its 2023 estimate valued ABH at about $500M, so she may no longer be a billionaire. She is a frequent podcast and interview guest on immigrant-founder stories. The web-search budget ran out before this profile, so it relies on Wikipedia and company sites.

name: Mian Mohammad Mansha
current_role: Chairman, MCB Bank Ltd; head of the Nishat Group (Pakistan)
profile: Born in Chiniot, Punjab, and educated at Hendon College in London, Mansha built his family's cotton-ginning business into the Nishat Group. It spans Nishat Mills (textiles), MCB Bank (acquired in 1992 privatisation), cement, insurance, hotels and power generation. In 2010 Forbes listed him as Pakistan's first billionaire.
interesting_fact: Forbes listed him in 2010 as the first Pakistani on its billionaires list. His group also bought two power plants in the late 2000s, adding an energy angle to its textile and banking base.
deep_cut_fact: He went to school at Sacred Heart Convent in Faisalabad before studying at Hendon College, London. In 1979 he built the textile complex at Nishatabad near Faisalabad that became the group's industrial base.
notes: Received the Sitara-e-Imtiaz in 2004 and has sat on the Atlantic Council board. The MCB and Nishat websites blocked automated access, so I could not pull a published IR/press email. MCB's investor-relations page and annual report should list one. The web-search budget ran out before this profile.

name: Pratap Reddy
current_role: Founder and executive chairman, Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd (Chennai)
profile: Born 1933 in Aragonda (now Chittoor district, Andhra Pradesh), Dr Prathap C. Reddy trained as a cardiologist in the UK and US before returning to India. In 1983 he founded Apollo Hospitals in Chennai, India's first corporate hospital chain, which grew into one of Asia's largest integrated healthcare groups. In his 90s he remains chairman, with his four daughters in senior roles.
interesting_fact: Apollo's first hospital in Chennai (1983) was inaugurated by then-President Zail Singh. Reddy received the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian honour, in 2010.
deep_cut_fact: After Stanley Medical College he did a fellowship at Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston and then ran research programmes at the Missouri State Chest Hospital before returning to India.
notes: Spelled 'Prathap C. Reddy'. He is 93 and alive per Wikipedia as of 2026. The Apollo site blocked automated access, so I could not extract a published IR/press email. Apollo's corporate communications team or the annual report is the route. The web-search budget ran out before this profile.

name: Vladimir Melnikov
current_role: Founder, owner and chairman of the board, Gloria Jeans (Moscow)
profile: Melnikov founded the Gloria cooperative in Rostov-on-Don in 1988 and the Gloria Jeans retail company in 1997. The business also manufactured for Western brands such as Levi's and H&M. After Inditex, H&M and Uniqlo left Russia in 2022 it expanded rapidly into their vacated space and now runs 700+ stores in Russia, Belarus and Kazakhstan. HQ moved to Moscow in 2016.
interesting_fact: In 2022 he gave 1 million rubles to each employee who had worked at Gloria Jeans for at least 10 years.
deep_cut_fact: His 1988 Gloria cooperative in Rostov-on-Don became the first officially recognised jeans maker in the Soviet Union.
notes: Russia-based. Check sanctions and reputational considerations before outreach. The Gloria Jeans site renders via JavaScript, so I could not extract a press email. The web-search budget ran out before this profile.

name: Xu Yi
current_role: Founder and president, Bilibili Inc. (Nasdaq: BILI; HKEX: 9626)
profile: Xu Yi, an early AcFun user known online as '⑨bishi', launched Mikufans.cn in 2009, which became Bilibili in January 2010. In 2011 he set up Hangzhou Huandian Technology to run the site. Bilibili grew from an anime/comics/games (ACG) community with 'danmu' bullet comments into one of China's largest video platforms, listing on Nasdaq in 2018. Chen Rui is chairman and CEO; Xu remains president.
interesting_fact: The name 'Bilibili' comes from a nickname for Mikoto Misaka, the heroine of the anime 'A Certain Scientific Railgun', and the site celebrates her birthday on its homepage every 2 May.
deep_cut_fact: Bilibili began on 26 June 2009 as 'Mikufans.cn', a fan community for the virtual singer Hatsune Miku, which Xu built while AcFun was suffering a month of downtime.
notes: Xu is famously low-profile; Chen Rui is the public face of Bilibili. Approaching through Bilibili IR is the realistic route. The web-search budget ran out before this profile.

name: Ina Chan
current_role: Private investor; shareholder in SJM Holdings, STDM and Macau Legend
profile: Ina Chan (Chan Un-chan), born in Macau, was a nurse hired to care for Stanley Ho's first wife after a 1971 car accident and is recognised as the late casino magnate's third wife. Her wealth comes from stakes in Macau casino operator SJM and Ho's former vehicle STDM, plus a holding in Macau Legend.
interesting_fact: She met Stanley Ho while working as a nurse caring for his first wife, Clementina Leitão.
notes: Very private, with no public role or published contact. She left the Forbes list after 2021. I found no death report but could not verify current status (the web-search budget ran out). Her wealth is tied to Ho family estate matters, so she is a poor fit for an entrepreneurship/energy podcast and I do not recommend outreach.

name: Hope Bryant
current_role: Vice Chairwoman (since 2011) and director, First Citizens BancShares, Inc. and First-Citizens Bank & Trust (Raleigh, NC)
profile: Hope Holding Bryant, 63, is a third-generation member of the Holding family that has led First Citizens Bank since Robert Powell Holding joined in 1918, and the sister of Chairman/CEO Frank B. Holding Jr. She joined the bank in 1985 and has been Vice Chairwoman since 2011. First Citizens became a top-20 US bank after buying CIT (2022) and Silicon Valley Bank (2023).
interesting_fact: First Citizens traces back to the Bank of Smithfield, opened on 1 March 1898 in Smithfield, NC, and has been led by her family for three generations.
deep_cut_fact: From 2006 to 2011 she was president of IronStone Bank, a former First Citizens subsidiary, before becoming Vice Chairwoman in January 2011. She has worked at the bank since 1985.
notes: The 2026 proxy publishes fcbdirectors@firstcitizens.com, routed via the Corporate Secretary, for messages to individual directors; address it 'Attention: Hope H. Bryant'. The SVB acquisition gives a tech/venture-banking angle. The country field was blank in the input; she is US-based.

name: Abigail Bennett
current_role: Heiress and shareholder of Constellation Brands; no executive or board role found
profile: Abigail Bennett is a granddaughter of Marvin Sands, who founded a small wine business in 1945 at age 21 that became Constellation Brands (Corona and Modelo in the US, Robert Mondavi, Svedka). Her wealth comes from her inherited stake. The family received $1.5B pre-tax in 2022 when it converted its high-vote shares. Her brother Zachary Stern is also a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Constellation's founder Marvin Sands started the business in 1945 at age 21. It now holds the US rights to Grupo Modelo's beer brands, including Corona and Modelo.
notes: Very private, with no public role found. She is not on Constellation's 2026 proxy board slate. Her uncles Robert and Richard Sands are the family's public faces. I found no published personal or office contact. The web-search budget ran out before this profile, so research was limited.

name: Fatma Tuba Yazici
current_role: CEO, Diler and Yazıcı Iron and Steel; principal shareholder, Diler Holding (Istanbul), as of the last Forbes update in 2018
profile: Fatma Tuba Yazıcı and her three sons became the largest shareholders of Diler Holding after her husband Recep Sami Yazıcı died in 2009. She became CEO of Diler and Yazıcı Iron and Steel, among Turkey's largest steel producers, and holds shares in listed Asil Steel. She sits on the Istanbul Chamber of Commerce's committee for iron-steel and hot-mill products.
interesting_fact: Forbes called her Turkey's only woman billionaire industrialist.
notes: Extremely private: per Forbes she grants no interviews and provides no photos so as not to be recognised on the street. The Forbes profile was last updated in 2018, so her current status is unverified. Diler Holding's websites did not respond, and the web-search budget ran out. Outreach is unlikely to succeed; any approach would have to go through Diler Holding corporate.

name: Chris Thomas
current_role: Co-founder and family owner, Thomas Foods International (Murray Bridge, South Australia)
profile: Chris Thomas co-founded T and R Pastoral with Bob Rowe in 1988, trading livestock before moving into feedlots and meat processing. The business bought the Murray Bridge abattoir in 1999 and became Thomas Foods International. It is now Australia's largest wholly family-owned red-meat processor, with five plants, 3,000+ staff and exports to 85+ countries. Day-to-day management has passed to the next generation.
interesting_fact: After a January 2018 fire destroyed the Murray Bridge processing line, TFI built a replacement plant on a new site about 8 km away, completed in May 2023.
deep_cut_fact: The company began in 1988 as 'T and R Pastoral', named for founders Thomas and Rowe, as a livestock-trading business before it processed any meat itself.
notes: Low-profile and largely retired from management; the managing director is a family member. The company site blocked automated access, so I could not extract a contact email. He was on Hurun's list only from 2018 to 2021. I could not verify current status because the web-search budget ran out.
